R000.function: Positions at the middle of multi-token units: partial digits of years and numbers, mid-word fragments of names and compounds, and function words inside noun phrases in encyclopedic prose. Fires on a token that is not yet complete or whose continuation is highly constrained.

R001.function: Prepositions, infinitive 'to', and the blank/digit tokens right before a year, in narrative history text; the next word is a time, place, or event complement.

R002.function: Connective glue tokens (to, in, commas, 'are', year-start spaces, header equals signs) in news/history/biography prose. Mixed syntactic positions with no single clear trigger.

R003.function: Function words and verbs that open a clause or modifier in reported or narrative statements (that, the, a, 's, returned, winning), where a description or outcome of an event follows.

R004.function: Names and titles in entertainment contexts (Bollywood, film, games, anime): fragments of personal names, film titles, and critic descriptions. Positions inside or just after a person or work name.

R005.function: Mid-sentence function words and verbs heading toward a complement or clause (that, which, to, of, seemed, occurs) plus digits in dates and measurements; a sentence mid-flow where more content must follow.

R006.function: Connectives inside mid-sentence relations (and, of, than, due, was, these) in expository history, with some digits in dates. Position where a linking word expects a noun phrase.

R007.function: Positions at the start or middle of a noun-phrase or clause after a preposition or verb (for, in, which, to, strategy, constructing), plus number onsets; abstract nouns of method or reaction in expository text.

R008.function: Word fragments of rarer words and names, wiki section-header equals signs, and mid-phrase nouns; sub-word pieces where the word is not yet complete.

R009.function: Prepositions, 'the', and 'to/of/than' following a verb or noun of access, development, or evidence, in abstract descriptive prose about societies, policy, or history. The next token is a noun phrase object.

R010.function: Numeric contexts: digits within years, dates, scores, statistics, and tabular lists, plus quantity words (total, several, BC). The text is giving a quantity, a date, or a record.

R011.function: Mid-sentence function words and adverbs (later, by, of, their, can, being, according) in descriptive prose about sport, reports and explanations. No sharp shared trigger.

R012.function: Structured biographical or reference formatting: names split into pieces, birth/death date digits in parentheses, wiki heading equals signs, list punctuation (colons, semicolons), and 'in the' taxonomic phrases.
R012.category: Names, life dates, headers, list punctuation

R013.function: Coordinating and boundary tokens (and, commas, periods, 'which', 'along with', closing quotes) that join items in a list or end a clause in expository text; year digits too.

R014.function: Punctuation closing or linking a clause: apostrophes of possessives (Madero's, deities'), sentence-final periods, commas after a noun, and '@' in number formatting. Tokens at a noun-phrase edge.

R015.function: Subword pieces of rare proper names, foreign-script bytes, and digits in dates or years. The token is inside a name or number that is not yet finished.

R016.function: Small function words and nouns mid-clause (more, an, back, was, in, that, took, coins, deities) plus digits; the token sits where a quantity or object phrase follows. Mixed, loosely coherent.

R017.function: Mid-phrase tokens in institutional and organizational descriptions (aviation, regulation, clubs, regions, cult centers): commas, 'and', 'that', and modifiers in lists or nested noun phrases.

R018.function: Punctuation and formatting tokens: commas, section-header equals signs, number separators like '@', quote marks, apostrophes in contractions, and digits. Structural glue of wiki-style text.

R019.function: Structural markers (header equals signs, year onsets, odd non-Latin bytes) and mid-name fragments, plus attribution or example words (stated, instance, particularly) in encyclopedic text.
